analysis.investment_thesis: Data Patterns is a rare Indian defence electronics pure-play with a 31.6% revenue CAGR and 33.1% net profit CAGR over 3 years, exceptional 43% operating margins, and zero debt — the kind of numbers that make a Fisher investor sit up straight. India's Atmanirbhar Bharat defence indigenisation drive provides a multi-decade structural tailwind that makes this a compelling long-term compounder despite the premium valuation.
key_strengths: Revenue growing at 31.6% CAGR (INR 311 Cr in FY22 to INR 708 Cr in FY25) with 43% operating margins — exceptional economics for a manufacturing company
Zero debt (D/E 0.00) with equity growing from INR 575 Cr to INR 1,508 Cr — pristine balance sheet funded organically
Deep product portfolio across radar, EW, IFF, avionics, and space systems creates genuine technical barriers and high switching costs with government defence customers
key_risks: Operating cash flow was negative in FY23 (−INR 17 Cr) and FY25 (−INR 90 Cr) — defence contract payment cycles cause severe working capital lumpiness
P/E of 79x and P/S of 20x price in near-perfect execution; any order delay, contract cancellation, or cost overrun will compress the multiple sharply
Customer concentration in Indian defence (primarily DRDO, Navy, Air Force) means budget cycles and procurement delays are existential quarterly risks
red_flags: Free cash flow was −INR 196 Cr in FY25 despite strong reported profits — earnings quality is inconsistent and receivables are likely building
Cash balance fell from INR 213 Cr (FY23) to INR 38 Cr (FY25) even as profits grew — capital is being consumed by working capital and capex faster than reported earnings imply
Very small revenue base of INR 708 Cr makes extrapolating 3-year CAGRs dangerous; order book visibility and execution timelines are difficult to verify externally
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Data Patterns is precisely the type of company I spent my career searching for: a technically specialised business serving a captive, long-cycle customer (the Indian defence establishment) with products that cannot easily be substituted. The combination of 43% operating margins, 31% revenue growth, and zero debt is extraordinary — it tells me management has built genuine pricing power rooted in proprietary technology in radar subsystems, electronic warfare, and space systems. The promoter stake of 42.41% aligns management interests squarely with long-term shareholders.

My primary concern — and it is material — is cash conversion. Profitable defence companies routinely show negative operating cash flow because government receivables stretch for quarters. The FY25 OCF of −INR 90 Cr and FCF of −INR 196 Cr alongside cash declining to INR 38 Cr signals the company may need external funding if the order execution cycle lengthens. At a P/E of 79x I am buying future earnings that must be delivered flawlessly. I would hold a focused position and monitor OCF conversion closely each quarter.
